findings.finding: The first two subjects now assert the same preservation-of-slavery decision. The narrowed SUBJ-20E4EBF24394 still includes free-colored rights evidence from its compound discovery record CHUNK-006-SUBJ-041. CHUNK-006-SUBJ-069 independently supplies the duplicated slavery subject.
findings.recommendation: Merge/reconcile the slavery records; keep free-colored citizenship distinct in meaning even if using one umbrella.

findings.finding: Post-narrowing edges imply Robespierre's rise supports preservation of slavery, place free-colored political rights under preservation of slavery, treat one duplicate as part of the other, and contrast Barnave with a decision he recommended. These are inconsistent with the source passage and the final node meanings.
findings.recommendation: Re-adjudicate all edges incident to SUBJ-20E4EBF24394 after fixing its identity. Do not repair labels without checking endpoints and relation types.

findings.finding: Anticolonial positions implies a broader opposition to colonial rule than the cited passage establishes. The inspected evidence concerns slavery and political rights of free people of color.
findings.recommendation: Use the narrower source-supported description: anti-slavery and support for political rights regardless of color.

findings.finding: Flexible censorship is represented, but the source's explicit paradox that public condemnation advertised books is absent from this meaning, stance and acceptable access; legacy SUBJ-721D8227847E preserves it.

counts.reproducibility_judgment: Legacy retains map/caption except source credit. Native uses whitespace count 20,083 minus 210 furniture/title tokens minus all 19 extracted map-page tokens = 19,854. Caption omission is verified; differing extraction/normalization is otherwise unresolved.
Legacy extraction count 10,088 lacks a tokenizer/version. Native Unicode tokens with line-end joining yield 9,970 but neither regex nor exact removal ledger is preserved here.

Legacy joins line-end hyphens and retains chapter title; native specifies pdftotext -raw whitespace tokens, excludes chapter number and retains heading. Different tokenization can account for some difference; no exact reproduction claimed.

Legacy has per-page counts, excludes chapter title and note calls. Native says extraction total less 150 furniture tokens, with no exact tokenization/removal ledger. A six-word difference is not evidence of semantic superiority.

Legacy retains map captions, legends and extractable labels while excluding raster-only labels from the token total. Native excludes dense map internals and Paris sectional gazetteer. Visual pages 127/129 confirm mixed captions, source credit, labels and gazetteer, requiring an explicit scope decision.

Legacy specifies Unicode tokens, joined line-end hyphens, lexical hyphen compounds as one, and excludes chapter title and note calls. Native specifies wc -w: 10,756 minus 183 running tokens = 10,573. The denominators use materially different token conventions.

word_count_review.conclusion: Neither six-chunk subtotal is a reproducible canonical denominator from the inspected artifacts alone. Both include method descriptions but lack a shared executable/tokenization specification and exact retained-region manifest. The differences do not determine benchmark choice.
word_count_review.lineage_note: Legacy CHUNK-001 original discovery (33 subjects) and v2 (120 subjects) retain the identical 19,778 count; this shows unchanged denominator metadata, not independent recount validation. Native CHUNK-001 explicitly marks its count as bounded_estimate.
recommended_exact_protocol: Bind exact PDF bytes, Poppler version, extraction flags and sidecar hash; process each owned source page once and never count context duplication.

Create a page/region ledger: retain body prose, substantive block quotations, chapter headings, substantive captions and any available substantive notes; exclude running heads, folios, note-call markers, source credits and bibliographic furniture. Fix these inclusion choices before counting.

Resolve maps explicitly: recommended common text denominator retains substantive captions but excludes cartographic internals, scales, key labels and the Paris-sections gazetteer. The p129 list is a 48-item numbered key keyed to map sections, with no independent table analysis; its function is cartographic even below the image. Inspect maps semantically in a separate coverage ledger. This is a proposed policy reconciliation, not permission to overwrite either frozen policy. If a different map rule is adopted, transcribe eligible raster text deterministically and apply it uniformly.

Normalize extracted Unicode with NFKC; remove soft hyphens; use a reviewed per-page join ledger for line-break hyphenation so lexical compounds are not silently changed. Keep both raw text hash and normalized retained-text hash privately.

Use Python 3 Unicode re with the frozen token expression r"[0-9]+(?:[.,][0-9]+)*|[^\W_]+(?:['’-][^\W_]+)*" after normalization. Numeric decimal/grouped expressions count as one; apostrophe/hyphen compounds count as one; dates/ranges beginning with numerals form separate numeric tokens. Publish boundary examples and freeze the implementation version. This recommended convention is not a claim that historical counts used it.

Publish page counts, chunk sums, excluded-region reasons, extraction warnings, and hashes; verify chunk sums equal the sum of owned page counts. Rerunning the exact code and retained-region manifest must reproduce the totals.

Recompute the source denominator independently of either subject count. For later density analysis use the same denominator for both, retain unrounded values, and disclose any region-policy sensitivity separately; do not use density to select or size the benchmark.
